source.title: LLM Persona Unlearning
source.authors: Ke-Mou Li; Zhuan Shi; Qi-Zhou Wang; Feng-Peng Li; Negar Rostamzadeh; Golnoosh Farnadi; Jian-Tao Zhou

record.file_problem: Full paper and appendix are present. Some table content is flattened, so values that cannot be assigned confidently to a model or metric are not extracted.
record.tranche_reason: The study tests whether target personas remain elicitable after weight editing, including under jailbreak-style prompts, conversation, translation, and new prompt wording. Its results refine the claim: residual accessibility varies by persona, while PACE retains high forgetting scores in most tested shifts. The target is persona behavior, not factual knowledge.
record.gate_note: The paper tests persona-policy suppression, not recovery of targeted factual knowledge. It tests no relearning-set fine-tuning, activation-direction ablation, or quantization. Rows for its prompting and elicitation robustness tests are included; values cited from other work are excluded. The paper's own Llama-3.1-8B Impolite diagnostic compares content suppression with persona expression, but those measures do not directly test any listed version, so they are recorded as findings fitting no version.
record.test_reason: The study does not test the claim. Every version concerns unlearned targeted knowledge: near-chance accuracy, hidden knowledge restored by relearning, ablation, quantization or prompting. This paper unlearns persona behaviour policies (sycophantic, hallucinating, impolite, apathetic, evil) and measures how strongly a judge sees the persona expressed (TF). That is a related but different construct. Its jailbreak, multi-turn, translation and new-prompt tests probe re-elicitation of a behaviour mode, not recovery of forgotten knowledge. PACE is a new unlearning method for personas, not a counter-method shown to resist knowledge-recovery attacks. These findings belong under fits_no_version. The paper cites WMDP and Who's Harry Potter only as background on content-oriented unlearning.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that content-oriented unlearning can leave a persona active or fake forgetting via generation collapse. PACE suppresses target personas across six models and five personas with good response quality, at moderate utility cost and with residual accessibility under stronger elicitation.
record.recipe_differences: PACE is a contrastive weight-training method using a persona direction, counterpart-relative erasure, and orthogonal anchoring. It is not a fine-tuning, ablation, quantization, or prompt-only recovery attack.
record.method_sensitivity: Recovery under Attack@5 differs by persona; Sycophantic and Hallucinating show larger TF drops. The study also varies elicitation format across multi-turn dialogue, translated prompts, and new question/instruction pools.

fits_no_version.finding: Under prompt-only elicitation shifts, PACE-edited Llama-3.1-8B persona suppression mostly holds but is incomplete for some personas. Attack@5 lowers TF to 75.5 (Sycophantic) and 70.5 (Hallucinating) while Impolite, Apathetic and Evil stay at 91.5–100. Multi-turn dips to 86.5 for Hallucinating. Translations and new prompts leave TF at 95–100.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Weight-level persona unlearning leaves residual, persona-dependent accessibility under adaptive prompting, analogous to shallow knowledge unlearning.

fits_no_version.finding: Content-level unlearning on the Impolite persona has two failure modes. NPO cuts reference-answer matching (ES 0.219 to 0.042) yet TF rises only 5.3 to 8.5. GA and RMU reach apparent TF of about 74–75 only through generation collapse (RQ about 1, with 19 and 3 of 250 responses gradable).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Content-based unlearning metrics can show forgetting while the underlying behaviour policy persists, or while generation collapses.

fits_no_version.finding: Under translated Impolite prompts, baseline NPO TF varies from 37.0 (English) to 91.0 (Chinese), with RMU and WGA lower (§F.2.1). No row records this.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Persona-suppression strength of content-unlearning baselines depends on prompt language.

record.problems: The robustness tests use Llama-3.1-8B and 50 questions per persona; the new-prompt test is also a 50-question, TF-only evaluation. The paper states that experiments use one training seed. Persona judgments are from an LLM judge; independent human assessment is identified as future work. The translated test uses machine-translated prompts, not independently authored native-language benchmarks. Some baseline and figure values are available only in figures or flattened tables.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted for the 60-row limit. Flattened Table 1 and Table 10 values not needed for the listed claim versions were not reconstructed. The paper's temporary direction-steering layer-selection probe is not an ablation attack restoring behavior after unlearning, so it was not recorded as a version-C result.

untested.parts: No targeted-knowledge accuracy, chance-level comparison, or knowledge-recovery attack.
No relearning or fine-tuning attack after unlearning. The authors list post-edit fine-tuning as future work.
No activation-direction ablation on unlearned models and no block-vs-delete analysis of knowledge. Steering is used only for layer selection before editing.
Prompting attacks target persona re-elicitation, not recovery of forgotten knowledge.
PACE is not evaluated against knowledge-recovery attacks of any kind.

record.verdict_notes: All row version links (V5/V6) were invalid and are set to none. None of the reader's labels stand, because the study targets persona behaviour rather than unlearned knowledge, and the versions concern knowledge recovery. The robustness tests use only Llama-3.1-8B, 50 questions, one training seed, and an LLM judge.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test whether targeted-knowledge accuracy reaches near chance while general ability is retained and attacks fail to recover that knowledge. It evaluates persona expression and utility instead.
No post-unlearning fine-tuning on unrelated, loosely related, or forgotten examples.
Uses a persona direction to train a weight edit, but does not ablate the direction after unlearning or establish that an edit only blocks access rather than deleting knowledge.
No quantization attack on unlearned weights.

Tests jailbreak-style wrappers, multi-turn elicitation, translations, and new prompts/questions. Does not test in-context provision of forgotten information or other languages beyond the reported translations.
Tests PACE against the reported elicitation shifts; does not test its resistance to fine-tuning, activation ablation, or quantization.
